title: Fast and Flexible Protein Design Using Deep Graph Neural Networks
authors: Alexey Strokach, David Becerra, Carles Corbi-Verge, Albert Perez-Riba, Philip M. Kim
datasets: Gene3D superfamilies (72.4M pairs); ProTherm; Rocklin miniproteins
evaluation_metrics: Sequence recovery (32-39%); accuracy on masked residues; experimental CD & NMR on designed de novo proteins
key_result: Demonstrates protein design framed as CSP; successfully designs de novo 4-helix bundles folded in vitro
limitations: Lower recovery than later models (33% vs 51%); relies strictly on 12A cutoff without 3D backbone frames
overlap_with_our_project: Directly provides the ProteinSolver formulation and baseline weights

title: ELASPIC2 (EL2): Combining Contextualized Language Models and Graph Neural Networks to Predict Mutation Effects on Protein Stability and Interactions
authors: Alexey Strokach, Carles Corbi-Verge, Philip M. Kim
datasets: VariBench; SKEMPI v2.0; ProTherm; SARS-CoV-2 spike
evaluation_metrics: Pearson r; Spearman rho; AUROC; RMSE
key_result: Shows ProteinSolver node/edge embeddings provide strong structural representations complementary to language models
limitations: Focused on delta-delta-G mutation effect rather than de novo generative sequence design
relevance: Demonstrates that ProteinSolver embeddings combine fruitfully with sequence language models
overlap_with_our_project: Demonstrates ensembling ProteinSolver features with modern models

title: Robust deep learning-based protein sequence design using ProteinMPNN
authors: Justas Dauparas, Ivan Anishchenko, Nathaniel Bennett, Hua Bai, Robert J. Ragotte, Lukas F. Milles, et al.
evaluation_metrics: Native sequence recovery (51.6%); perplexity; experimental crystallization; cryo-EM
key_result: SOTA sequence recovery; 200x faster than Rosetta; highly robust to backbone noise in wet lab
limitations: Can experience mode collapse at low sampling temperatures; does not natively optimize diversity or multi-objective trade-offs

title: Learning inverse folding from millions of predicted structures
authors: Chloe Hsu, Robert Verkuil, Jason Liu, Zeming Lin, Brian Hie, Tom Sercu, Adam Lerer, Alexander Rives
task: Inverse folding & zero-shot variant effect prediction
evaluation_metrics: Native sequence recovery (51.3%); Spearman rank correlation on deep mutational scanning (DMS)
key_result: Demonstrates scaling inverse folding with predicted AlphaFold structures; strong zero-shot fitness correlation
limitations: High memory footprint; large parameter size (142M); slower inference than ProteinMPNN

title: PiFold: Toward effective and efficient protein inverse folding
authors: Zhangyang Gao, Cheng Tan, Stan Z. Li
key_result: Matches/exceeds ProteinMPNN recovery with 10-70x speedup via one-shot prediction
limitations: Non-autoregressive decoding can struggle with long-range epistatic co-occurrence constraints
overlap_with_our_project: Benchmarking target for modern inverse folding

title: Benchmarking Evaluated Protein Inverse Folding Models
authors: Zhangyang Gao, Cheng Tan, Stan Z. Li
model: Multi-model (ProteinSolver ProteinMPNN PiFold ESM-IF1 GVP etc)
datasets: CATH 4.2; TS50; TS500; CASP15; de novo backbones
evaluation_metrics: Sequence recovery; scRMSD; scTM; ESMFold pLDDT; diversity; inference time
key_result: Direct independent comparison showing ProteinSolver has 33% AAR vs ProteinMPNN 51.6%; ProteinSolver exhibits distinct diversity profile
limitations: Benchmark only; did not propose hybrid or ensemble mechanisms combining models
relevance: Most comprehensive independent comparison of ProteinSolver vs modern baselines
overlap_with_our_project: Direct comparison of ProteinSolver vs ProteinMPNN on identical benchmarks

title: Combining Language Models and Inverse Folding for Antibody Design via Inference-time Weighted Ensembles
authors: Richard Shuai, Jeffrey A. Ruffolo, Jeffrey J. Gray
task: Antibody sequence design & CDR loop inpainting
evaluation_metrics: CDR sequence recovery; perplexity; in silico humanness; foldability
key_result: Inference-time linear weighting of ProteinMPNN and language model logits improves recovery and biophysical validity
limitations: Restricted to antibody domain and IgLM language model; does not evaluate GNN-GNN fusion or ProteinSolver
relevance: Validates inference-time ensembling of inverse folding models
overlap_with_our_project: Closest proof-of-concept for inference-time logit combination

title: De novo design of protein structure and function with RFdiffusion
authors: Joseph L. Watson, David Juergens, Nathaniel R. Bennett, et al., David Baker
task: De novo backbone generation + sequence design + validation
relevance: Established canonical modern paradigm: diffusion backbone -> ProteinMPNN sequence -> AlphaFold2 validation
overlap_with_our_project: High experimental success but standard sequence generation produces tight clusters of low-diversity sequences
evidence_status: Establishes the canonical pipeline we must benchmark against

title: ProteinZero: Self-Improving Inverse Folding via Online Reinforcement Learning
task: Self-improving inverse folding via online RL
evaluation_metrics: Design failure rate (scRMSD > 2A); sequence diversity; ddG reward
key_result: Reduces design failure rate by 36-48% and explicitly introduces embedding diversity regularizer to prevent mode collapse
limitations: Requires expensive RL training loop; computationally heavy
relevance: Directly explores diversity-aware inverse folding with structural validation
overlap_with_our_project: Closest work addressing diversity-aware inverse folding

title: Illuminating Protein Sequence Spaces with Quality-Diversity Algorithms and Gradient-Informed Emitters
task: Quality-diversity search in discrete sequence space
datasets: GFP fitness; GB1 fitness; antimicrobial peptides
evaluation_metrics: Pareto front volume; QD-score; sequence diversity; Hamming distance
key_result: MAP-Elites with gradient emitters finds diverse high-fitness sequence archives overcoming epistatic local optima
limitations: Evaluated primarily on 1D fitness landscapes rather than 3D structure-conditioned inverse folding
relevance: Provides algorithmic foundation for quality-diversity candidate selection

title: Boltz-1: A fully open-source biomolecular structure prediction model
authors: Jeremy Wohlwend, et al. (MIT Jameel Clinic)
evaluation_metrics: lDDT; RMSD; TM-score; complex contact accuracy
key_result: Open-source model matching AlphaFold3 performance on biomolecular complexes and monomers under MIT license
limitations: Computationally demanding for batch inference of thousands of candidates without GPU acceleration
relevance: Provides modern open-source structure validation oracle (alternative to AF2/AF3)

title: Atomic-level protein design using LigandMPNN
task: Context-aware sequence design with small molecules and nucleic acids
evaluation_metrics: Recovery in binding pockets; crystallographic validation of enzyme active sites
key_result: Extends ProteinMPNN to coordinate-conditioned ligand environments with high atomic precision
limitations: Focuses on ligand binding contexts rather than sequence diversity or ensembling with distance GNNs
